title: alert_handler: register and field names in the class configuration steps
conditions: Configuring alert class A at startup, as the programmer's guide's initialization steps describe; the same holds for classes B to D.
C3 and C5 record a value after reset; the other settings are encoded as 1 if the statement about the design holds and 0 if it does not.

requirements.note: Initialization step: the number of alerts accumulated before escalation.

requirements.text: Determine length of each escalation phase by setting [`CLASSA_PHASE0_CYC`](../data/alert_handler.hjson#classa_phase0_cyc) accordingly
set the [`CLASSA_CTRL_SHADOWED.E0_EN`](../data/alert_handler.hjson#classa_ctrl_shadowed) bit accordingly (default is enabled).
program it via the [`CLASSA_CTRL_SHADOWED.E0_MAP`](../data/alert_handler.hjson#classa_ctrl_shadowed) values if it needs to be changed from the default mapping (0->0, 1->1, 2->2, 3->3).
requirements.note: The phase to escalation signal mapping.

requirements.text: Optionally lock the class configuration by writing 0 to [`CLASSA_CTRL_SHADOWED.REGWEN`](../data/alert_handler.hjson#classa_ctrl_shadowed).
enable the ping timer mechanism by writing 1 to [`PING_TIMER_EN`](../data/alert_handler.hjson#ping_timer_en).

MAP_E0 resets to phase 0 in each class (MAP_E1 to MAP_E3 reset to 1, 2 and 3).

CLASSA_CTRL_SHADOWED is locked by CLASSA_REGWEN, as are the class's other configuration registers.

generated_from_same_input: D1 to D3 and D5 to D12 are in Earl Grey's alert_handler.hjson, generated from hw/ip_templates/alert_handler/data/alert_handler.hjson.tpl, from which the register RTL and registers.md are also generated; those are not counted as further evidence. D4 and D13 are in the hand-written register wrapper template. R1 to R6 are in the hand-written template document; Earl Grey's generated copy has the same lines.
finding: Every setting the steps describe agrees with the design: escalation signals are enabled after reset, the default mapping is 0->0, writing 0 to the class lock bit locks the configuration, and writing 1 enables the ping timer. But six names are wrong: four registers have been renamed with a _SHADOWED suffix (CLASSA_ACCUM_THRESH, CLASSA_PHASE0_CYC and PING_TIMER_EN here, CLASSA_CLR in the interrupt handling steps), E0_EN and E0_MAP are EN_E0 and MAP_E0, and the class lock is the register CLASSA_REGWEN, not a field of CLASSA_CTRL_SHADOWED.
missing_information: This case reads the register description and the register wrapper; it does not simulate the alert handler.
ambiguities: The names are close enough that a reader may find the right register; the links in R1, R2 and R6 point to anchors that registers.md does not have.
out_of_scope: CLASSA_CLR in the interrupt handling steps (line 85), which has the same renaming.
Shadowed registers must be written twice; the documents say so elsewhere.
